newsitem.title: USA: Polaris sees 1997 net income topping 1996.
newsitem.headline: Polaris sees 1997 net income topping 1996.

text.p: Polaris Industries Inc, after reporting lower sales and profits for the second quarter, said it expects net income for the year to be well ahead of 1996's record level.

"Continued improvement in our gross margins and second half sales approximating last year's second half, should offset a slower first half, resulting in 1997 full-year net income well ahead of 1996's record level," the company said.
Retail sales of personal watercraft have been slower than expected again this season, although the company is in a better inventory position than last year, it said.
"We are expecting slower retail demand after many strong seasons of snowmobile sales and are adjusting our production plans for the 1998 model year accordingly," Polaris said.

Polaris on Thursday reported net income of $13.3 million on sales of $249.9 million for the second quarter ended June 30, compared to net income of $16.3 million on sales of $317 million in the same three-month period a year ago.
Retail sales of all-terrain vehicles (ATVs) continued to grow with U.S. sales particularly strong and North American field inventories coming down to targeted levels.
Interest in the company's new Victory motorcycle is strong at the dealer and consumer level, the company said.
